title: Zambia's Copper Push: Record 890,346 Tonnes, a $1.47bn IMF Deal, a 3m-Tonne Goal | The Six, Ep. 22
lede: Zambia mined a record 890,346 tonnes of copper in 2025, still short of its one-million-tonne target. Six years after Africa's first pandemic-era default, it has reached terms with official creditors and bondholders on a restructuring of about $13 billion in external debt, and agreed a new $1.47 billion IMF programme. The goal now is three million tonnes a year by 2031.
keyPoints: Zambia missed a $42.5 million Eurobond coupon in late 2020, becoming Africa's first sovereign default of the pandemic (Reuters).
Official creditors co-chaired by China and France agreed terms on $6.3 billion of loans in June 2023; bondholders agreed terms in March 2024 (Center for Global Development).
The 2022 IMF programme ended in January after disbursing about $1.7 billion; a new 36-month, $1.47 billion programme reached staff-level agreement in October and awaits Board approval (IMF).
Copper output rose to a record 890,346 tonnes in 2025; first-half 2026 output was up only 0.45%, and the government projects 930,000 tonnes for the year (Ministry of Mines; Reuters).
LME copper hit a record $14,875 a tonne on Sept. 10 and closed at $12,471 on Nov. 18, about 16% lower (International Copper Association Australia).
